September 2009 # Chinese consumption – Real or apparent? - Chinese copper demand remains robust, but issues over the accuracy of Chinese copper data make answering the question in the title difficult. With some sectors outperforming expectations, we have raised our estimate for full year Chinese growth to 14%. Demand elsewhere appears to be bottoming out. - Mine supply is seeing few disruptions and grew y-o-y in H1 despite previous cutback announcements. However, Q2 results confirm that refined production growth is being constrained by the difficulties some smelters have in selling sulphuric acid. - The copper price raced up by another $1,000/t to over $6,000/t over the past month, well ahead of the fundamentals. We expect prices will be particularly volatile over the next month, with a possibility that the rally could be extended by some postsummer holiday restocking in September. |The supply/demand

Fore|cast pro|duction|allows for|potential|disrupti|ons| © 2009 CRU International Limited **confidential** September 2009 Copper Monitor **www.crumonitor.com** # Many questions, but few answers As usual, August has seen subdued spot market trading. So, with little to report on that front, in this Monitor we outline the key issue facing the global copper market. How much of this

year’s record level of refined cathode imports into China is being translated into real refined consumption (i.e. melted by semi-fabricators, the consumption definition used by CRU and the copper industry)? 

Over the first seven months of 2009, refined imports in China rose by almost 1.3Mt y-o-y and apparent consumption by about 1.4Mt.  The prohibitive cost of re-exporting cathode means that Chinese imports are effectively lost.  Therefore, whether this copper is actually consumed or not is of secondary importance to the rest of the world, as the global copper market now effectively operates on a China vs. Ex-China basis. 

We have been calling for declining Chinese cathode imports and visible increases in cathode stocks for several months.  Tentative signs of this only appeared in August.  Reported import data show a fall of 87,000t in refined cathode in July from the June record.  At the same time, SHFE stocks rose to over 80,000t (as of 21<sup>st</sup> August).  Admittedly, these shifts are tiny compared to a Chinese market that is on course to consume over 5Mt of refined cathode this year.  However, we have also heard from traders that off-warrant stocks in China have increased.  In addition, Chinese media report speculative physical buying by small investors in the country (including pig and duck farmers!), although they are not a major reason for the rise in Chinese imports. These reports about small investors may, however, indicate that China is in a commodities bubble (apparent consumption in China is extraordinarily high across many commodities, not only copper) that is about to burst. 

Bubbles are a regular occurrence in China as people have few investment opportunities and tend to see asset bubbles as a chance to make their fortune.  The fuel for this bubble (if that is what we are seeing) is most likely coming from the extremely easy lending policy of Chinese banks.  For now it is a safe bet that the government will maintain a loose monetary policy through end 2009 at least, to support their 8% GDP growth target. Therefore the trigger for bursting a Chinese commodities bubble is unlikely to come from a liquidity squeeze. 

## **Signs of investors outside of China increasing exposure to copper** 

China is not the only source of fresh speculative money in commodities.  Barclays Capital estimates that commodity assets under management on behalf of institutional and retail investors increased by 19% q-on-q in Q2.  In the first two months of Q3, copper open interest on the LME has risen along with prices, indicating a further build up of new investment long positions.  Whether this increase is part of a global bubble is an open question, and we are only likely to see a significant correction to the price once the last bear capitulates.  When that last “known unknown” will be is anyone’s guess.  The one thing of which we are certain is that copper prices will remain volatile over the next few months. 

## **Chinese consumption – the key

to the puzzle** 

The list of questions about Chinese copper consumption is a long one and this overshadows issues in the rest of the world when looking at market fundamentals.  As addressed repeatedly over the last few Monitors, developments in scrap availability will remain a key determinant of refined consumption.  The level of total scrap imports (both official and smuggled) and the copper content of scrap are big assumptions, as data is patchy in both scope and quality.  Copper semi-fabricated products production data in China poses another question.  This was not a major issue up to and including 2007, as most measures of semis production correlated well with one another and with other measures of economic activity (e.g. market data tallied with end-use indicators from NBS), but since 2007 they have been on divergent courses.  There are 2 sets of monthly Chinese semis production data, from the CNIA (China Non-ferrous Industry Association) and the NBS (National Bureau of Statistics).  The CNIA is the one that seems to be the most widely followed, as it is seen to be the best and most reliable source.  Another question is about the growth in semis production

capacity, which we estimate amounts to a name-plate 900,000t in 2009.  This new capacity will require working stocks, the total amount of which is another open question. 

For the time being, we have raised our full year 2009 Chinese refined consumption forecast to 14%.  This is on the basis that end-use growth is performing well in the wirerod sector and outperforming our previous estimates in some other sectors, such as automotive (due to tax incentives), construction (easy lending policy) and home appliances (scrappage schemes and a hot summer that has boosted air conditioner sales). 

## **Rest of world consumption hitting bottom** 

#### Chinese consumption data - Many questions, few answers 

Known and admitted problems with double counting remain unresolved 

Unknown level of SRB stocks, purchases and sales Unknown level of scrap stocks Unknown level of semis inventory Unknown level of cable production, cable stocks Uncertainty over non-semis producer purchases of cathode (military, utilities, merchants) Uncertainty over role of middle men, bonded & unbonded warehouses Monthly semis production data do not add up to cumulative Semis data reported only on a gross weight basis Semis data not broken down by copper/alloy, scrap/refined, wirerod/brass mill Huge number of reporting fabricators (thousands) – with many new entrants/closures and people only operating part of the year 

The lack of spot market activity due to summer holidays means there is little direction as to where copper demand is heading at the moment.  We therefore need to look to other indicators to gauge the direction of near term demand.  In the US, housing sales picked up in July and consumer confide

nce in August.  However, any recovery in the broader economy that will underpin the recovery in US copper demand is likely to be weak, as unemployment will continue to rise well into 2010 and corporate spending will be constrained by modest profitability growth and tight credit conditions.  Furthermore, the residential mortgage market (and therefore construction demand for copper semis) still faces significant restructuring, with 9.2% of mortgages in arrears and a further 4% in the process of foreclosure (the highest levels since records began in 1972). 

As for Europe, forward looking macroeconomic indicators point to a market that has now hit the bottom. Orders in the Eurozone industrial sector were up by 3.1% m-o-m in June, and the latest Purchasing Managers Index rose back to 50, indicating that industrial output is no longer contracting.  Given that Germany, France and Italy avoided the worst of the housing bubble, the fact that continental Europe is pulling out of the economic recession earlier than the US makes sense.  However, we will have to wait until September and October for signs of how well the early economic recovery phase is transferring to the copper market in Europe and whether copper demand in the US has really hit bottom. 

Given that most copper consumers are maintaining low inventories, we do expect a restocking boost to cathode demand at some stage in the recovery.  However, the severity of the economic downturn and the still relatively tight credit markets mean that restocking will most likely kick in only once consumers are seeing a sustained increase in their order levels. 

Meanwhile, refined consumption in the rest of Asia is benefiting from government stimulus measures across the region and exports to China.  India is showing good growth as its relatively low levels of exports as a percentage of semis production means that a rebound in broader domestic economic growth is translating into semis production and hence higher refined consumption.  In addition, India has also seen a similar dynamic to China on the scrap front.  Lower imports of scrap into the country have resulted in higher refined consumption than previously estimated.  We have therefore raised our 2009 copper consumption growth forecast for India to 8.6% in this month’s Monitor. 

## **Limited disruptions result in strong growth in mine production** 

We have seen few signs of mine supply disruptions so far this year, so there is a distinct possibility that we will see less than the usual collective level of underperformance by mining companies of about 1Mt again this year. Disruptions due to strikes, if they occur, are more likely to affect next year’s mine production, as most labour agreements are only coming to an end late in 2009.  With prices as high as they have been, production in H1 2009 is currently estimated at 7.7Mt, up by 175,000t y-o-y (on an undisrupted basis).  Grasberg has been the largest single mine contributing to growth, up by 210,000t

y-o-y. Escondida’s 241,000t decline more than © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 12 September 2009 Copper Monitor **www.crumonitor.com** offsets this, however. Among the rest, Codelco has provided much of the net growth, as output at its mines rose by over 100,000t from 716,000t in 2008 to 822,000t this year, due to the ramp up of Gaby and undisrupted production at El Teniente (compared to last year). The only significant production news has been at smelter/refiners. Q2 results show that there were sulphuric acid related cutbacks in production at a number of smelters, some of which had not been previously announced. Output was down at Asarco’s US plant, Xstrata’s Canadian and Chilean smelters, as well as Anglo’s Chilean smelter. These reductions in throughput saw production some 10-20% lower than originally planned. Of course, with Chinese demand remaining strong, we have seen Mitsubishi return to full capacity after the fire at Onahama in March. The determining factor for refined output will, therefore, remain on smelter/refiners as the drive to increase capacity utilisation is counteracted by cut backs due to sulphuric acid. ## **Prices up to new 2009 high but premiums slip** Prices fell below $5,400/t in late July, but then staged a rally to a new 2009 high of $6,460/t for 3-month material by 14th August. Since then prices retested lower support levels but have generally traded above $6,000/t. Official prices of both cash and 3-month fell below $6,000/t only once through to 26th August. Many traders are on holiday this month, so volumes on the LME are lower and the impact of new trades, as a result, has been amplified. The copper market is firmly in the summer doldrums, with little spot market activity reported anywhere and modest increases in LME inventory levels this month. Some traders reported that earlier in August there was better spot demand in Europe, although this was not universally reported. If that happens, then the low levels of inventory at consumers mean that there may be a pick up in premiums, most likely in Asia and Europe as LME warehouses there have only 23,000t and 62,000t, respectively (as of 26th August), for consumers to tap into, if needed. ## **Price direction? Anyone’s guess as they are so far ahead of fundamentals** We have adjusted Chinese consumption higher but, given the arbitrage window closed in May and the lag in shipment, imports should ease further over the coming months. Continuing reports of the build up in offwarrant stocks also suggests that imports should decline. We believe the price has run ahead of this summer’s fundamentals. We expect prices will be particularly volatile over the next month, with a chance that the rally could be extended by some post-summer holiday restocking in September. Nevertheless, energy cable demand has performed better than for other wire and cable segments during the financial crisis. Partly this is because wire and cable used in power transmission and infrastructure has benefitted from stimulus packages. However, it is also due to the long timeframe for many power cable purchases and commercial construction projects, which means that production has not responded quickly to the downturn. There are risks that energy investment spending could slow over the next few years, particularly in developed countries. Commercial construction is now contracting in North America and Europe. Power infrastructure provision in developed countries is largely from private companies, some of whom are likely to cut back investment programmes. Future prospects for the energy cable sector are likely to rely on the strength of growth exhibited in developing countries, particularly China and India. ## **Winding wire: leading indicator** Winding wire is used in the manufacture of motors and transformers for a wide range of applications including transportation, power transmission, industrial motors and consumer appliances. s|e mont|hs, seas|onally| © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 9 of 12 September 2009 Copper Monitor **www.crumonitor.com** # Industry News ## **Production** - **Minera Escondida** reported that it has completed repairs to the SAG mill at its Laguna Seca concentrator at **Escondida** . The mill resumed operations on 2nd August. As a result, Escondida has ended its _force majeure_ on concentrate shipments from the mine that went into effect on October 10, 2008. In 2009, Escondida is expected to produce 690,000t of copper in concentrates and 310,000t of copper cathode. - It was reported, on mid August, that **Grupo Mexico** (Mexico) said that it will raise its bid for **Asarco** (USA) to US$2.2B cash. Few days later, as a response, **Sterlite Industries** (India) rose up its bid to a level that can pay cash unsecured creditors. Grupo Mexico is currently competing against Sterlite Industries for control of Asarco. - On 13th August, **Newmont** announced the start-up of operations at its gold-copper **Boddington** project in Western Australia. Boddington will produce 40,000t/y of copper in concentrates at full capacity. In 2009, CRU expects Boddington to produce 15,000 of copper in concentrates. - Unionised employees went on strike at **Vale’s** Canadian operations in **Sudbury** (12th July) and **Voisey’s Bay** (1st August) after rejecting the company’s offers for new three-year collective labour agreements. At Sudbury, the strike affects about 3,100 workers, while at Voisey’s Bay 120 employees are involved. Voisey’s Bay operations were temporarily closed in July and were due to restart on 1st August. Sudbury began an eight-week shutdown on 1st June and was due to restart on 27th July. On 3rd August it was reported that Vale declared _force majeure_ at Sudbury. Vale is considering restarting operations at Sudbury using management and non-union workers. In 2009, Sudbury and Voisey’s Bay were expected to produce 38,000t and 19,000t, respectively, of copper in concentrates. - On 30th July, **Copper Mountain Mining

Corporation (CMMC)** announced that it had signed definitive agreements with **Mitsubishi Materials Corporation** for Mitsubishi to acquire a 25% interest in the **Copper Mountain** project in British Columbia, Canada, for US$28.75M. **Mitsubishi** also agreed to purchase all copper concentrate output from the mine.  Copper Mountain is scheduled to restart operations in 2011 and will produce 43,000t/y of copper in concentrate. 

- **Quadra Mining** announced that has started operations at its **Franke** project (Chile) and expects the first shipment in September.  Quadra Mining purchased this project from **Centenario Copper** in February 2009.  Franke is expected to produce 30,000t/y of copper cathode. 

- On Tuesday 11<sup>th</sup> August, labour unions at **KGHM** (Poland) held a two-hour strike over government plans to further privatise the company.  The proposal considers selling about 10% of its current 41.79% share.  Workers had warned they would hold a longer stoppage if the government goes ahead with this proposal.  In 2009, KGHM is expected to produce 422,000t of copper in concentrate and 496,000t of refined copper. 

- It was reported that the **Baluba** mine (Zambia) has re-started mining copper as the majority of rehabilitation work has been completed.  New owners, **China Non-Ferrous Metals Corporation (CNFMC)** , aim to start full production in December 2 09.  CNFMC is also developing the **Mulyashi** project and plans to invest a total of US$400M in both the Baluba and Mulyashi projects.

- Workers at **BHP Billiton** ’s **Spence** mine in Chile have asked for a 5.5% wage increase as the collective labour negotiations begin and are threatening to go on strike.  The contract is due to expire on 26<sup>th</sup> September 2009.  The result of this negotiation will be a precedent for other large mines in the region - **Escondida** (BHP Billiton, **Rio Tinto** , **JECO** and **IFC** ) and **Chuquicamata** ( **Codelco** )- whose workers are also threatening industrial action.  In 2009, Spence is expected to produce 185,000t of copper cathode. 

- **Cape Lambert Iron Ore Limited** announced the divestment, via an Initial Public Offering (IPO), of its **Lady Annie** mine in Queensland (Australia).  Cape Lambert Iron Ore acquired Lady Annie earlier his year as part of the acquisition of **CopperCo** and is advising now to retain between 5% and 10% of the new company.  In 2009, Lady Annie is expected to produce 5,000t of copper cathode. 

## **Exploration and Development** 









- **Codelco** submitted an Environmental Impact Assessment to extend operations at **Division Salvador** (Chile).  The current operations are due to end in 2011 as the current sulphide reserves are not economically exploitable.  The project aims to start construction in 2010 to mine copper oxides at the **San Antonio** deposit.  It will requi

re an investment of US$220M and has reserves of 170Mt @ 0.52% Cu.  The project would produce 30,000t/y of copper cathode at full production over a 20year mine life.  In 2009, Salvador is expected to produce 38,000t of copper in concentrates and 15,000t of copper cathode. 

- On 25<sup>th</sup> August, Mongolia’s Parliament approved amendments to four laws, within it a sunset provision to cancel a 68% windfall profits tax on copper and gold effective on 1<sup>st</sup> January 2011. These changes are very important for the development of **Invanhoe Mines Ltd’s Oyu Tolgoi** project. **Rio Tinto** owns a 9.95% stake in Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.  Earlier in August, the company and the government were negotiating terms for the legal framework for foreign investors in Mongolia. The company and the government are working towards signing the Oyu Tolgoi Investment Agreement, in which the government would obtain a 34% interest in the project.  The Oyu Tolgoi deposit is one of the largest copper ore resources in the world and CRU expects it to produce some 360,000t/y of copper in concentrates, with start up not expected before 2013. 

- It was reported that **Tongling Nonferrous Metals Group Co** announced that it plans to invest US$64M to develop a new copper mine in Anhui province.  Environmental permits are pending.  The project is due to start-up in 2012 and will produce 5,227t/y of copper in concentrate. 

- On 10<sup>th</sup> August, **Anvil Mining** and **Trafigura Beheer** announced a strategic alliance of US$200M funding package (debt and equity finance) to recommence the construction of **Kinsevere Stage II** SXEW project in the Katanga province (DR Congo).  The transaction is pending of approval of the Toronto Stock Exchange.  Kinsevere Stage II is planned to begin commissioning in late 2010 and produce 60,000t/y of copper cathode. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 



- In early August, **Doe Run Peru** (a unit of the US based **Renco Group** ) informed the regulatory authorities of Peru its intention to restructure its operations after months of financial difficulties.  Doe Run Peru owns and operates the La Oroya smelter, which has paralysed operations – expect the copper circuit, which is fed by copper concentrates from its Cobriza mine – since June after banks cut

## **Consumption** 







- **Nexans** announced that it has signed an agreement to sell its Montreal wirerod mill to **AmRod Corp** , a copper wirerod producer based in New Jersey, USA.  The closing of the transaction is scheduled to take place in Q4 2009, subject to a number of regulatory conditions. The sale is consistent with Nexans’ plan to reduce foreign sales of copper wirerod and focu

s on its core wire and cable businesses. Other Nexans’ North American facilities will not be affected by the transaction. 

- Japan's copper wire and cable shipments rose in July to 58,200t, the highest level in eight months, up 8.9% from June (and up 30% from May), but down 21 % from 73,244t a year ago, according to the **Japanese Electric Wire and Cable Makers' Association** , with the domestic construction sector still particularly hard hit. The 305,818t  shipped from January to June is the lowest six-month level since the first half of 1975 and is 27% down y-o-y; automobile sector shipments fell 46.3% y-o-y to 25,985t, those to the electric machine and appliance sectors fell 42.4% to 58,974t and those to the construction and wholesale sectors fell 17.9% to 140,492t. 

- China's Jiangxi Province, which is seeing rapid growth in its copper industry, produced 511,900t of copper semis in H1 2009, up 14.3% y-o-y, according to government sources.  New projects commissioned in the province in recent months include: a 100,000t/y secondary smelter (stage 2) for **Fuwang Copper of Zhejiang Zhongwang Co. Ltd** , a 50,000t/y copper semis project for Jiangxi Junmao Co. Ltd., a 100,000t/y secondary smelter and a 10,000t/y copper semis, plate, strip and hardware project for **Jiangxi Jinhui Copper** , a 54,000t/y copper semis project for **Jiangxi Sanchuan Copper Co. Ltd** and a 4,000t/y Cu-Ni-Zn project for **Jiangxi Yihuang Yongsheng Copper Co. Ltd.**
